title: Short past passive participles: куплен, написан, открыт

blocks.text: If the verb of a sentence is transitive, the idea may be expressed in two ways: if we want to emphasize the performer of the action, we use the active voice; if we want to emphasize the object or target of the action, we express the same thought in the passive. *Студент купил книгу. — Книга куплена студентом.* In the passive construction the performer of the action is expressed by the instrumental case (студентом).

The new relations are expressed in Russian by a special form of the verb which is called the short past passive participle (PPP). It is used only as a predicate in passive constructions. Past passive participles express the idea of a completed action and are almost exclusively formed from perfective transitive verbs.

They form the short PPP from the first person singular future perfective by dropping the ending -у or -ю and adding -ен, -ена, -ено, -ены (stressed: -ён, -ена́, -ено́, -ены́): куплю — куплен, куплена, куплено, куплены; приведён, приведена, приведено, приведены. In most verbs the stress remains on the same syllable as in the 2nd person singular: бросишь — брошен; предложишь — предложен; принесёшь — принесён; but: изменишь — изменён. The changes of consonants of the future also appear: спрошу — спрошен; замечу — замечен; отпущу — отпущен; посажу — посажен; куплю — куплен; возвращу — возвращён; приглашу — приглашён.

They form the short PPP from the masculine past tense by dropping -л and adding -н, -на, -но, -ны: сделал — сделан; потерял — потерян; осмотрел — осмотрен. The stress shifts one syllable to the left if in the infinitive it is on the last syllable: написать — написан; связать — связан; осмотреть — осмотрен; and remains unchanged in all other cases: услышан, сделан.

a) Prefixed derivatives from some monosyllabic verbs: убит, разбит, открыт, закрыт, покрыт, скрыт, помыт, побрит. b) Verbs in -нять: понят, снят, занят, принят. c) Verbs in -нуть: вынут, повёрнут. d) Verbs in -деть: надет, одет, раздет. e) забыт, начат, взят. The PPP from съесть is съеден. The verb «вернуть» has no PPP; it is formed from «возвратить»: возвращён.
Both are used as predicates only; both are not declined; both agree in gender and number with the subject. To express tense the verb быть is used exactly as with short adjectives:

items: The garage will be built in a year.
The book may have been taken yesterday.

blocks.text: For each set of two parallel English constructions there is only one in Russian: The letter is written / has been written — *Письмо написано.* The letter was written / had been written — *Письмо было написано.* Passive constructions with the indirect object as subject are impossible in Russian: I was given a book — *Мне дали книгу. Мне была дана книга.* Verbs that take a preposition, or are intransitive in Russian, can only be translated actively: *Над ним смеялись. За доктором послали. Ему помогли друзья.*
Further sentences, so that every pattern above is practised: from the library's public-domain books.
